key_insight: Uniformly interior η-feasible directions enable finite-direction searches for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization over general closed convex sets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports derivative-free constrained optimization when exact line searches and structural access to the feasible set are available.
method: Optimize smooth-minus-convex objectives without accessing their decomposition, using exact line searches along feasible segments.
Build search directions with an η-direction oracle or noise-augmented randomization.
Control direction-spanning coefficients and feasible step lengths to establish stationarity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees—not empirical benchmarks—including finite-time approximate d-stationarity, PDM convergence rates, and almost-sure d-stationarity of randomized accumulation points.
watch_item: Exact line searches and constraint-geometry access may be costly; rate guarantees also depend on regularity assumptions and uniformly bounded direction-set sizes.
paper_title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
